A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the analytical model is able to provide the time constant and the compensation factor of the measuring circuit, and it is able to be used for the design of a high-impulse-current measuring shunt with cage configuration.
the proposed model can be used for the design of high-impedance shunts, and it can be applied to the analysis of the transient response of a rail gun launcher.

a high-impulse-current measuring shunt with cage configuration can be designed with the use of a simple first-order equivalent circuit model and that the time constant can be minimized by optimizing the geometrical parameters of the cage and the sensing wires.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a cage structure can be used to obtain a fast response time for the measuring shunt.
the use of the cage configuration allows the reduction of the inductance by a factor of 10 with respect to the classical coaxial configuration.
a high-impulse measuring shunt can be designed with a time constant in the range of 1-5 ns and a resistance in the range of a few ohms.
